data.body:
Landed as Gerrit change 1660 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, 0 unresolved), merged to main as b0a25a318f9.

WHAT THE DEFECT WAS. `dc_store_copy_repo` fetched the live `tickets` branch with
`subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, check=True)`. The capture routes git's stderr into a
buffer; `CalledProcessError`'s string form then reports only the exit status. Live run
31587452003 therefore recorded `exit status 128` and nothing about the cause. The `git archive`
and `git ls-tree` calls beside it had the identical shape.

THE FIX. New module-level `run_git(argv, cwd, *, runner)` keeps the capture (the fixture
consumes `git archive`'s stdout as bytes) but performs the check itself, raising `RuntimeError`
carrying the joined command — hence the remote and branch — the exit status, and git's verbatim
stderr. All three call sites route through it. With the failure finally legible,
`fetch_tickets(...)` adds bounded retry (FETCH_ATTEMPTS=3, backoff injectable) on the one
network call. Policy is retry-then-FAIL as planned, never retry-then-skip: a genuine
misconfiguration still reds the lane rather than silently dropping the store-copy cells.

VERIFICATION, ALL REPO-TIER. `tests/unit/test_dc_store_copy_fetch_diagnostics.py` loads
`_dc_fixtures.py` by path (the pattern from test_live_dc_isolation_controls_59b2.py) and drives
the helpers with a stubbed `subprocess.run`: the failure message carries a distinctive git
stderr line verbatim plus remote/branch/status; a stub failing once then succeeding proves the
retry returns and backs off; an always-failing stub proves the attempt count is capped at
FETCH_ATTEMPTS and the final raise still names git's stderr. Two anti-change-detector controls:
a negative control constructing `CalledProcessError` exactly as check=True does, asserting its
string form does NOT contain the stderr (this is what makes the primary assertion meaningful),
and an AST check over the parsed call sites asserting no `subprocess.run` in the fixture pairs
`capture_output` with `check` — parsed rather than grepped so this module's own docstrings,
which necessarily quote the bad shape, do not trip it.

Gates on the merged tree: 31 unit cells pass, make lint pass, make typecheck pass (509 files),
684 dc/jira-selected unit tests pass. No cell deleted, skipped or xfailed.

FOLLOW-UP, recorded and deliberately not an AC: confirming on a live run that
test_outbound_unassign_round_trips passes — or now fails with git's actual reason — needs a Live
External Integration run, which is operator-spend. The next scheduled run reads the improved
message; if it still errors, the log will finally name the cause and that becomes its own
ticket. That is the whole point of doing the diagnostic first.
